assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ab initio molecular dynamics unified electronic-structure theory with atomic motion and opened simulation of bond breaking, liquids, water and reactions in condensed phases. It is a true game-changer for theory that connects quantitatively to experiment, and a precondition for modern simulation-based chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Two-person paper of 1985 with a clean, widely accepted credit; both names fit a fair prize, and Parrinello's later work is not needed to justify recognition.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent adoption across chemistry, materials and biology; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to tie Parrinello to metadynamics or ML potentials instead of this single discovery.
Relies on my own recollection of the history rather than verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues is a new pharmacological modality that has already produced clinical candidates and a mechanistic explanation of thalidomide-class drugs. Clearly new, with real consequences.
assessment.attribution: The 2001 PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) and later VHL-ligand and cereblon work (Ciulli, Handa, Ito) make credit multi-branched; at most three can share and the choice among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and many clinical trials, but no approved PROTAC drug as far as I know, so the clinical payoff is still maturing.
uncertainties: Allocation between PROTAC pioneers and molecular glue/cereblon discoverers is unresolved.
Compound discovery whose parts may merit different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable in vivo and enabled siRNA therapy and mRNA vaccines at global scale. A chemistry-driven game-changer with unmistakable real-world consequences.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer; Cullis's group led the core ionizable-lipid and formulation work, with Anderson for lipidoid optimization. Allocation among at most three is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Validated by approved siRNA and mRNA products; recognition is timely though the mRNA part was recently recognized in Medicine (2023).
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may weigh against it.
Precise priority of individual lipid designs is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair into another without double-strand breaks, a simple, original chemical idea that is now in clinical use. It is a genuine game-changer built on chemistry-driven protein engineering.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual driver; the junior co-authors (Komor, Gaudelli) are credited but a single-laureate or Liu-led configuration is most defensible. CRISPR itself was already recognized in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed by many groups and early clinical data, but long-term clinical outcomes are still emerging, so timing is on the early side.
uncertainties: Whether the Chemistry committee views genome editing as sufficiently distinct from the 2020 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies to silicon-like levels within about a decade, a new class of material with large consequences, in the spirit of MOFs being a completely new material class.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first showed the perovskite sensitizer; Park (solid-state cell) and Snaith (meso-superstructured and thin-film) were decisive in efficiency. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also have claims, making a three-person limit painful.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is well confirmed; stability and commercialization are unresolved, so the prize may be premature.
uncertainties: Long-term device stability and toxicity of lead.
Fair allocation among six credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis transformed biology and medicine through cheap sequencing, with chemistry at its core (reversible terminators, clonal arrays).
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived Solexa chemistry; Rothberg, Mayer and Ju represent competing or complementary technology branches, so a Solexa-based pair is defensible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with huge independent impact; the long delay is a concern for timing but not for merit.
uncertainties: Whether commercial platform leaders deserve credit over the Solexa inventors.
Boundary with the 1980 and 2018 prizes on sequencing and evolution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory resolved the Levinthal paradox and gave a quantitative framework for folding that is tested by experiment, which I value as theory tied to measurements.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson built the funnel picture; Dill's hydrophobic and lattice-model work and Fersht's experiments complicate credit. Three names fit but excluded contributors are significant.
assessment.maturity: Concept is widely accepted and confirmed by folding experiments and later by structure prediction, but its impact is largely conceptual now, partly overtaken by the 2024 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 Chemistry prize on protein structure prediction.
Who counts as decisive among theorists and experimenters.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of the spliceosome clarified how a large RNA-protein machine catalyses splicing, linking structure to RNA catalysis, which appeals to my interest in ribosome-like mechanisms.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann's biochemistry and Shi's cryo-EM structures were decisive; Stark and Nguyen contributed key structures, and the earlier splicing discoveries were recognized in 1993 and 1989.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed across organisms, though mechanistic detail by simulation or kinetics is still developing; the discovery is moderately mature.
uncertainties: Is this structural biology better suited to Medicine or Chemistry?
Mechanistic quantitative understanding is still limited.
